_about: Why each class and relation exists, the question it answers, and who confirmed it.

Policy.alternatives: Policy as a Constraint kind: rejected, authority and scope differ. GovernanceBody class: deferred to the workflow vocabulary.
Policy.question: Which rules must the product obey, who enforces them, and what is affected? (G6; Gate 3 review)
Policy.why: A policy prescribes behaviour and has an authority and an enforcing role, which a budget or timeline constraint does not; two people would populate a shared class differently.

Constraint.alternatives: One Concern class with a kind attribute: rejected, constraints, assumptions and risks have different lifecycles and owners.
Constraint.question: What constraints is it built under? (B4)
Constraint.why: A constraint is imposed from outside and limits requirements and releases; it has a source and a lifecycle distinct from an assumption or a risk.

Assumption.alternatives: Merged into Constraint or Risk: rejected, an assumption is a belief to check, not a limit or a threat.
Assumption.question: What assumptions is it built under, and which could invalidate the plan? (B4)
Assumption.why: An assumption is validated or invalidated over time and decisions rest on it, so its state change must propagate; that needs a node with history.

Risk.alternatives: A fourth Dependency class: rejected, no question yet traverses to external systems or partners. Add it when one does.
Risk.question: What are the risks and external dependencies? (E1)
Risk.why: A risk threatens something, is mitigated by something, and can block a release; an external dependency is modelled as a risk kind because what matters is what happens if it fails.

constrains.alternatives: A closed list of classes per side: rejected, two ontologies extending the same base could not both add to it.
constrains.question: What does this limit apply to?
constrains.why: A limit is only actionable when it names what it limits. One relation with an open side rather than a closed list of classes, so independent ontologies that extend this one compose without redeclaring it; the engine refuses two siblings widening the same relation.

relies_on.alternatives: A closed list of classes per side: rejected, two ontologies extending the same base could not both add to it.
relies_on.question: What are we taking for granted here?
relies_on.why: When an assumption is invalidated, everything resting on it must be found. One relation with an open side rather than a closed list of classes, so independent ontologies that extend this one compose without redeclaring it; the engine refuses two siblings widening the same relation.

threatens.alternatives: A closed list of classes per side: rejected, two ontologies extending the same base could not both add to it.
threatens.question: What is at risk?
threatens.why: A risk register that does not name its subjects cannot be acted on. One relation with an open side rather than a closed list of classes, so independent ontologies that extend this one compose without redeclaring it; the engine refuses two siblings widening the same relation.

mitigated_by.alternatives: A closed list of classes per side: rejected, two ontologies extending the same base could not both add to it.
mitigated_by.question: What reduces this risk?
mitigated_by.why: Shows which decision or requirement exists because of a risk, and which risks have no answer. One relation with an open side rather than a closed list of classes, so independent ontologies that extend this one compose without redeclaring it; the engine refuses two siblings widening the same relation.

applies_to.alternatives: One constrains relation for both: rejected in the duplicate audit. A closed list of classes per side: rejected, two ontologies extending the same base could not both add to it.
applies_to.question: Which rules must the product obey, and what is affected? (G6)
applies_to.why: Split from constrains so an agent never confuses a resource limit with a prescribed behaviour that has an authority. One relation with an open side rather than a closed list of classes, so independent ontologies that extend this one compose without redeclaring it; the engine refuses two siblings widening the same relation.

enforced_by.question: Who enforces this rule?
enforced_by.why: A policy with no enforcer is a wish; the enforcing role is who to ask.
